page: Amazon Web Services r7i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by fourth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (model 8488C). Featuring a 64-bit x86 architecture, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The processor architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache, along with native support for advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). It is provisioned with 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Hardware-level benchmarks reflect strong throughput and compute capability. The instance delivers a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 87,164.85 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,127.0, with exceptional performance in cryptographic encryption (89,289.07) and ray tracing tasks. In-memory throughput is reinforced by large uncached memory read bandwidth measuring 228.17 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 95.44 GB/sec. In database operations, the instance registers 30,332.14 on PassMark database testing and sustains 98.08 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware matrix extensions enable high prompt processing throughput across small and medium language models.

A key architectural consideration is storage configuration: the r7i.24xlarge includes no bundled local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent and temporary data disks. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps and lacks integrated GPU acceleration. In terms of cost efficiency, its dense allocation of 768 GB DDR5 RAM alongside 96 dedicated vCPUs offers favorable operational efficiency for consolidating memory-heavy architectures onto a single node. The r7i.24xlarge is particularly suited for large in-memory databases such as Redis or SAP HANA, distributed data caching layers, enterprise relational databases, big data analytics, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
